purpose: Machine-readable decomposition of this repo's own validation so failures are attributable to a named validator, and so a repair that genuinely fixes a validator's defect can be declared next to it.

profiles.release: Every leaf validator reached by `npm run validate:release`, plus the query-atlas gate that guards the evidence the atlas publishes against.
profiles.core: The page-level matrix only. Fast pass for content edits.

repair_policy: repair_command may only be declared when the command regenerates the exact artifact whose defect the validator detects. A repair is never declared to make an unrelated failure disappear; validators whose failures require human judgement are left with no repair and are reported by name.

validators.detects: Content or configuration that does not belong to the Porch & Party operating profile.
Stray, orphaned or non-canonical files in the published tree.
Internal agent/prompt instructions leaking into published HTML.
Empty table cells in published HTML.

Published pages missing the blocks an answer engine needs to quote and act on them: a direct answer, an h1 that carries the query, tables without empty cells, and one quote-request conversion path. Coverage for checklist, comparison table, concrete numbers, named sources, FAQ and JSON-LD is measured and reported.
Required files, canonicals, entity footers, legal links, internal hrefs, JSON-LD wellformedness and llms.txt extraction surfaces across every published page.
validators.no_repair_reason: Composite page-level matrix. Its failures (missing canonical, broken href, missing footer, malformed JSON-LD) are authored defects with no single regenerator. The one derived-artifact defect it also covers - sitemap desync - is attributed precisely by the sitemap-coverage validator below, which does carry a repair.

validators.detects: sitemap.xml out of sync with the published HTML tree in either direction.
validators.repair_rationale: scripts/generators/update_sitemap.js rewrites sitemap.xml by walking the same HTML tree this validator walks. It is the regenerator of the exact artifact whose staleness is the defect.

validators.detects: Corruption or absence of the 100k opportunity reserve: missing shards, sha256 mismatch, duplicate ids/queries, undeclared geography, wrong disposition, wrong record count.
validators.repair_rationale: build_max_fanout.mjs writes data/authority_scale/fanout_100k/ and its index.json - the exact shard corpus and manifest this validator hashes and counts. Regeneration is deterministic under AUTHORITY_RUN_DATE.

validators.detects: Violations of the authority-scale governance contract across the admission registry, operational window, velocity governor/decision and the accepted-output freeze.
validators.no_repair_reason: Spans artifacts owned by several different actions, two of which (authority:scale:freeze, authority:publish) are governance decisions with publishing side effects rather than regenerations. Running them to clear a validation failure would be a cadence change disguised as a repair.

validators.detects: KPI claims not backed by the observed surfacing ledger.
validators.no_repair_reason: The ledger is measured evidence. Nothing in the repo may generate it, and generating it would be fabrication.

validators.detects: Scoreboard counts that disagree with the citation-yield observation ledger, and a velocity decision that disagrees with velocity health (upshift or ceiling change while health is UNKNOWN).
validators.repair_rationale: build_citation_yield_feedback.mjs recomputes the scoreboard directly from the observation ledger (fixing scoreboard_truth), and evaluate_velocity.mjs recomputes the velocity decision from velocity health under its stated safety law - unknown always holds, only explicit failure downshifts (fixing upshift_on_unknown / changed_on_unknown). Both are derivations of the exact artifacts the validator compares; neither invents observations.

validators.detects: Published pages that do not meet the citation-yield page quality patterns.
validators.no_repair_reason: Fails on page substance. No generator in this repo rewrites page substance, and none should do so unattended.

validators.detects: data/authority_scale/page_improvement_plan.json missing, thin (<10 route plans), or carrying plans with no recommended improvements.
validators.repair_rationale: build_improvement_plan.mjs writes that exact file from the candidate backlog. If the plan is genuinely thin after rebuild the validator stays red, which is the correct outcome.

validators.detects: data/authority_scale/territory_health.json missing a required territory or reporting a thin public surface count.
validators.repair_rationale: build_territory_health.mjs writes that exact file by counting the live public surfaces. A territory that is genuinely thin stays red after the rebuild - the repair refreshes the measurement, it cannot fake it.

validators.detects: Missing .build distribution artifacts, or an IndexNow batch that does not match sitemap.xml exactly.
validators.repair_rationale: build_distribution_artifacts.mjs writes .build/indexnow-batch.txt, .build/indexnow-priority.txt and .build/distribution-manifest.json, deriving the batch from sitemap.xml. batch_sitemap_mismatch is precisely the staleness this command clears.

validators.detects: Violations of R1-R5 of the search-intelligence truth contract, including silent green on a degraded provider and any lane write to a protected publishing path.
validators.no_repair_reason: The only writable artifact in the lane (authority_feedback_receipt.json) comes from `search:feedback --write`, which applies authority feedback derived from live provider truth. Running it unattended to clear a red validator would manufacture feedback state with no provider reachable - exactly what R4 forbids.

validators.detects: Query evidence missing a tier or source_type, a publishable atlas entry on a non-publishable tier or with no volume, and a query_atlas.json that is absent or stale against the evidence file.
validators.repair_rationale: build_query_atlas.mjs writes data/authority_scale/query_atlas.json from data/queries/evidence/evidence_queries.json. The validator's own failure text says 'run the atlas build first'. This is the pairing that closes the loop after queries:ingest writes new measured T1 evidence.
